source.title: Understanding the Modality Gap: An Empirical Study on the Speech-Text Alignment Mechanism of Large Speech Language Models
source.authors: Bajian Xiang; Shuaijiang Zhao; Tingwei Guo; Wei Zou

record.file_problem: The text appears complete; some figures and tables are flattened, but the study and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports that cosine similarity and Euclidean distance give different alignment patterns, refining the claim that measured representation alignment is a single, unambiguous quantity. It examines speech-text alignment within LSLMs, not convergence between independently trained models.
record.gate_note: The relevant results measure speech-text representation alignment and how alignment metrics relate to the modality gap. Benchmark-only performance comparisons and results cited from other studies are not rows. The embedding interventions report downstream QA accuracy, not convergence itself; those rows are recorded as findings outside the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures speech-vs-text representation similarity inside one LSLM. A shared LLM backbone and speech adapter are trained on purpose to align speech with text. It never compares independently trained models, seeds or separate vision/language models, so none of V1–V7 is tested. The cosine-vs-Euclidean divergence shows metric dependence for a different construct: within-model cross-modal alignment, not cross-model convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add three points: the authors call the gap mainly a speech-text alignment problem (about 16.5% of the 25% drop); they say token-level APS correlates more strongly with the gap than sequence-level metrics; and they call token-level alignment the key mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Within-model speech-text comparison using sequence- and token-level cosine and Euclidean metrics, plus post-hoc embedding interventions; not an explicit replication of either named original source.
record.method_sensitivity: Cosine similarity and Euclidean distance give different alignment trends and token-path statistics. The metric-to-performance-gap correlations vary with full versus LoRA fine-tuning and between Llama and Qwen families. Layer depth and training checkpoint also change the reported alignment measures.

fits_no_version.finding: Within LSLMs, speech and text representations grow more aligned in cosine with depth while Euclidean distance also grows. Token alignment paths under the two metrics agree for only about 59% of tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-model cross-modal alignment in speech-language models is metric dependent: direction converges while magnitude diverges with depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-averaged similarity and APS predict the speech-text performance gap. R² is high under LoRA (0.75–0.95) and low under full fine-tuning (0.15–0.53).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-modal representation similarity predicts the modality performance gap in LSLMs, more reliably under LoRA.

fits_no_version.finding: Angle projection of the least-aligned speech tokens raises sd-qa accuracy in most settings, while length normalization mostly lowers it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-hoc directional alignment of speech tokens to text tokens can improve LSLM speech QA.

record.problems: The primary study uses English, single-turn dialogue with synthetic speech, and a limited set of architectures. The authors say broader validation on larger models and novel alignment strategies is needed. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the listed results. Some layer-wise trends are presented graphically without exact values.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4's separate curves for each primary model configuration and checkpoint, Figure 8's per-configuration training trajectories, and Figure 9's exact layer-wise values were not extracted individually; the stated aggregate trends are recorded in R1-R3 and R19-R20. Benchmark-only speech/text score comparisons and external-model performance table results were omitted because they do not measure representation convergence.

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models across scale or capability.
No separate vision and language models on image-caption pairs; speech and text share one trained LLM.
No cross-model feature or circuit comparison.
Metric dependence is shown only for within-model speech-text alignment, not for convergence between models.
No cross-model alignment or tests of its causes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked rows to V6. However, V6 concerns convergence between models, and here the alignment is within a single model and deliberately trained. No pairs of independently trained models are compared, so I reclassified the study as not testing the claim. It does not cite the Platonic Representation Hypothesis or convergent-learning work.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare independently trained models across architectures, objectives, data, size, or capability.
Studies speech and text, not vision models and language models on paired images and captions.
Does not compare networks trained from different initializations or analyze shared features or subspaces across seeds.
Does not test mapping representations between different models, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
Does not compare recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
Tests cosine similarity against Euclidean distance for speech-text alignment. It does not test neighbour-count settings or out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not compare alignment between independently trained models or test whether shared training data or objectives explain such alignment.

rows.value: Increases consistently with depth; later training checkpoints have higher similarity across layers.
rows.note: The text describes this trend across the models and training paradigms shown in Figure 4.
rows.check: Within-model speech-text cosine similarity after alignment training; not convergence between models.

rows.measure: Euclidean distance between sequence-mean speech and text representations
rows.value: Distance increases with depth, gradually in shallow layers and more rapidly in deeper layers.
rows.note: The authors describe increasing distance despite the increase in cosine similarity.
rows.check: Within-model speech-text Euclidean distance; not cross-model convergence.

rows.subject: All primary LSLM configurations (aggregate trend stated by the authors)

rows.note: The stated checkpoint trend is qualified as slight and does not reverse the depth-wise increase.
rows.check: Checkpoint trend of within-model distance; not cross-model convergence.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Cosine versus Euclidean measures of speech-text alignment in the tested LSLMs
reader_labels.reason: Cosine similarity rises with depth while Euclidean distance also rises, and token alignment statistics differ between metrics; the results show metric-dependent descriptions of alignment (R1, R2, R10, R11, R12, R19, R20, R21, R22, R23).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Relationship between alignment metrics and modality gap across training regimes and model families
reader_labels.reason: The reported metric-to-gap correlations vary across full fine-tuning versus LoRA and across Llama and Qwen families; APS correlations also vary by regime and family (R4-R9, R13-R18).
